# Full-thermal local cone transfer theorem

Derived here, 2026-11-02. Not a theorem quoted from the weight-reduction literature. Chain convention: C2 --d2--> C1 --d1--> C0, qubits in degree 1, X generators columns of d2, Z generators rows of d1. All algebra is over F2. Hamiltonian violation energies are J_g(1-S_g)/2, not -J_g S_g.

## 1. Constructive local contraction

Suppose the enlarged complex A is a direct sum of local blocks A^x,A^q,A^z plus attachment differential δ, with block differential d0. Each block has at most M coordinates in total, and attachment edges follow the original Tanner incidence. Block homology is one-dimensional in degree 2,1,0 respectively and zero otherwise. Attachments strictly lower the stratum x→q→z (an x→z attachment is harmless). The induced adjacent homology maps are the actual original check matrices.

This is the **all-degree**, not merely H1, structural input supplied by Hsieh–Li–Lin v2 Sections 2.4, 4.1.2 and 5.2. The vanilla local-cone construction is sufficient here; distance-amplifying dummy faces may be used only with the same contractible-cone and tree-product certificates. A modified gadget with additional endpoint homology is NOT covered by the exact preimage formula below. The construction has new check weight ≤5 and qubit degree ≤6 (Theorem 4.6). Retain every original check coordinate, including redundant checks; this is not Gaussian elimination of the global check set.

Within each finite block choose a normal-form contraction (p,i,h) by finite-field elimination:

 pi=1, p d0=0, d0 i=0, d0 h+h d0=1+ip, h²=hi=ph=0.

These maps never leave their blocks. Since h preserves stratum and δ strictly lowers it, (hδ)^3=(δh)^3=0. Define

 I=(1+hδ+(hδ)²)i,
 P=p(1+δh+(δh)²),
 H=(1+hδ+(hδ)²)h.

The elementary finite homological perturbation identity gives

 PI=1, P D=d P, D I=I d,
 DH+HD=1+IP, PH=HI=H²=0,

where D=d0+δ and the effective d is pδi+pδhδi+pδhδhδi. The terms containing two or more δ vanish after p: they go from stratum x to z while lowering chain degree by only one, whereas the retained homology degrees differ by two. Thus d=pδi is exactly the source differential, with no hidden effective incidence.

Every matrix entry involves at most three neighboring blocks. Consequently support radius is bounded by two Tanner edges plus block diameter. Both row and column norms are bounded and computable from finite blocks.

# Exact thermal fibers and a sharp no-free-lunch test

Violation-energy convention H=Σ_j J_j(1-S_j)/2. Write B_j=βJ_j and q_j=e^(-B_j).

## Exact disjoint-fiber theorem

This is elementary exact parity summation, closely related to classical decoration transformations; no historical novelty is asserted. Its use here is as a stringent full-temperature certificate, not a new code theorem.

Assume a surjective endpoint chain projection P has each column either zero or a unit coordinate vector. Its nonzero columns partition the fine check coordinates into disjoint nonempty fibers F_a. Assume the full endpoint homotopy, so fine validity is precisely P s'∈S, with S the source allowed-syndrome space. No independence of the **physical allowed syndromes** is assumed.

Sum the unconstrained product weights over each fiber at parity s_a. The even/odd partition sums are

 Z_a(0/1)=(1/2)[∏_(j∈F_a)(1+q_j) ± ∏_(j∈F_a)(1-q_j)].

Therefore the marginal on old syndromes is **exactly**, on every allowed s∈S,

 Pr(s) ∝ 1_(s∈S) exp[-Σ_a B_eff,a s_a],

 tanh(B_eff,a/2)=∏_(j∈F_a)tanh(B_j/2),
 e^(-B_eff,a)=tanh[Σ_(j∈F_a)atanh(q_j)] ≤ Σ_(j∈F_a)q_j.

Zero columns contribute a syndrome-independent partition factor. Redundant source checks are retained through the indicator of S. All auxiliary excited states have been summed; no low-energy truncation or ground projector appears. At uniform B_new and fiber size ≤r, **B_new≥B_old+log r** suffices for B_eff,a≥B_old exactly. The equality choice is B_new=2atanh[(tanh(B_old/2))^(1/r)], asymptotic to B_old+log r at large B_old.

Both endpoint projections must satisfy this fiber property to get this conclusion in both Pauli sectors. A fiber property for only one CSS matrix does not certify a quantum thermal memory. More generally, any separately proved decoder theorem for the exact correlated parity marginal can replace the singleton-column condition, but such a theorem must retain its actual charge and entropy.

## Why generic cone equivalence does not imply the hypothesis

For a three-stratum cone reduction, P0=p0+p0δh0+p0δh0δh0. Internal fine checks in a qubit or opposite-color check cone can project to multiple old checks. Ground-space equivalence gives neither disjoint fibers nor independence of those contributions. # Same-resource comparator and quantitative ledger

## Established alternatives before new machinery

- **Hastings, On Quantum Weight Reduction, arXiv:2102.10030v3 (corrected 2021 construction).** General CSS copying/gauging/thickening/coning gives weight ≤5 for LDPC inputs with constant overhead and constant distance loss. This is already a decisive comparator to a weight-180 implementation. Its code-parameter conclusion is not full Gibbs equivalence. https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.10030
- **Hsieh–Li–Lin, arXiv:2510.09601v2 (Oct 2026).** Symmetric local cones give weight ≤5, qubit degree ≤6, O(n w² log w) qubits and an amplified distance with uniformization/expanderization. Its vanilla Theorem 4.6 suffices for fixed-w local replacement; the three-stratum presentation permits the explicit finite contraction used here. Use corrected v2, not v1. https://arxiv.org/html/2510.09601v2
- **Sabo et al., PRX Quantum 5, 040302 (2024).** Classical-input reduction yields weight ≤6 for hypergraph/lifted-product codes and can use much less overhead than general Hastings reduction. The declared sheaf family is not supplied as such a product, so this cannot simply replace its Hamiltonian. https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.05228
- **Subsystem/circuit constructions.** Bacon–Flammia–Harrow–Shi provide sparse subsystem codes from Clifford circuits. Gauge generators are not commuting stabilizer energies; a Hamiltonian made of their sum need not have the Gibbs syndrome law used here. Measurement-based gauge fixing, protected symmetries, and noiseless subsystems change the resource/noise contract. https://arxiv.org/abs/1411.3334
- **Local Clifford/subdivision.** Exact conjugation U(H+H_aux)U† preserves the full spectrum and Gibbs state, but replacing conjugated high-weight generators by another low-weight generating set generally changes the Hamiltonian and Gibbs law. Ordinary cell subdivision can have the exact disjoint-parity property; simultaneous quantum cone reduction requires checking both endpoint maps.

Fine independent thermal defects conditioned on P0 b in S push forward to the exact correlated coarse marginal, which need not equal the old Gibbs law. Opposite-sector endpoint I2^T and decoder R'(s')=I1 R(P0 s')+H0 s' transport the ideal logical interface. Disjoint nonempty parity fibers obey q_eff=tanh(sum atanh q_j)<=sum q_j, so B_new>=B_old+log r suffices, using violation-energy units. This is not universal: translation by a valid fine syndrome tau bounds the coarse-fiber energy difference by E_tau. Duplicate redundant source generators force J_new>=r J_old/d_f when exact source Gibbs suppression is retained.
